To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

alpha-tricalcum phosphate bone cement is improved with respect to its mechanical strength by the addition of acrylamides and ammonium polyacrlyates, which are added in the form of an in situ polymerizable liquid.

the addition of ammonium polyacrylic and acrylamide as liquid reducers in the setting reaction of alpha-TCP cement increases the compressive and the tensile strength of this cement by 149% (55 MPa) and 69% respectively (21 MPa) in comparison to the original cement.
the mechanical strength of alpha-Tcp bone cement is increased by 149 and69% by adding acrylamide 20 wt% and ammonium poly acrylate 1 wt% to the mixing liquid.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a new generation of bone cements based on alpha-TCP, which can be easily prepared and applied to fill bone defects of any size and shape, and can be reinforced with polyacrylamides, which are biocompatible and biodegradable, to increase their strength and toughness.
the design and development of a new alpha-TCP bone graft with a higher mechanical strength.
the development of a new bone cement with improved mechanical properties, which can be used in bone repair and bone substitution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of acrylamides and ammonium poly-acrylates to alpha-TCP bone cements is a very promising approach to increase their mechanical strength without affecting their osteotransductivity.
alpha-TCP cement modified with acrylamide/PA has the potential to be used as a bone substitute in load-bearing applications.
the addition of AA and AP to alpha-TCP bone cements increases its mechanical strength by the formation of an entanglement composed by CDHA crystals and a polyacrylate network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of acrylamamide and ammonium polyacetate to the liquid of alpha-TCP cement, which causes an increase in the mechanical strength of the cement, does not affect the setting reaction, but it reduces the size of crystals and the porosity of the final product.
alpha-TCP cement can be modified by the addition of acrylamides and ammonium polyacrlyates to obtain a bone substitute with mechanical properties similar to those of human cancellous bone.
the addition of acrylamid and ammonium poly-acrylate to alpha-TCP bone cements improves its mechanical strength, without affecting its osteotransductivity and biodegradability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alpha-TCP cement can be modified to increase its mechanical properties without altering the setting reaction and the nature of the product, CDHA, which is a key feature of this material.
the addition of acrylamid and ammonium polyacetate to alpha-TCP bone cements can be used as an effective way to improve its mechanical properties without compromising its osteotransductivity.
the mechanical strength of alpha-TPC bone cement can be increased to a level similar to that of human cancellous bone, by the addition of acrylamides and ammonium poly-acrylate to the liquid phase.
